checks.note: It apologizes clearly: "I'm so sorry your kettle arrived with a cracked lid again" and "I completely understand your frustration."
It never mentions a refund or money back and doesn't hint at one. The only fix offered is a replacement "at no cost to you," which means a free replacement, not a refund.
It offers a replacement directly: "sending a replacement right away, at no cost to you."
The body, including greeting and sign-off placeholders, is about 100 words. Adding the subject line brings it to about 108, still under 120.
The tone is warm and friendly. It names the repeat problem ("again," "a third time") and the customer's loyalty ("After four years with us," "sticking with us all these years").

unasked_content: Asking for a photo before the replacement ships adds a hurdle for a customer who is already fed up after two broken kettles. That cuts against the friendly, make-it-right tone the person asked for, and it makes "right away" less true.
